text:
Hana: design sync  playground streaming UX — stop vs pause affordance + token footprint + prompt-library pairing.
Hana: TL;DR users confuse tiny streaming fragments for a hung model. instead of showing raw fragments forever, collapse into a single compact 'stream paused' chip after 600ms of low throughput. chip shows token count and a primary action (Resume/Regenerate).
Derek: +1 to the 600ms threshold. Question: should the chip say "Resume" or "Continue" when runtime supports resumable streams? Resume implies picking up where it left off.
Jonah: If can_resume true -> label = "Resume streaming"; else label = "Regenerate output". We should show the verb explicitly to avoid ambiguity.
Izzy: Accessibility: screen readers should not read the entire stream. strategy: keep the chunk region aria-live=polite, and when we collapse write a short announcement once: "Stream paused, 9 tokens buffered. Actions available: resume, regenerate, copy." Make the chip focusable (tabindex=0).
Hana: microcopy for the chip itself (visual):
- "Stream paused — 9 tokens"
- "Streaming paused: 9 tokens buffered"
- "Output paused (9 tokens)"
Pick which reads best visually.
Derek: I like "Stream paused — 9 tokens" (short + dash).
Jonah: Also propose an optional chevron to expand buffered fragments if the user wants to inspect partial text. keeps the default compact.
Izzy: Tooltip/accessibility nit: tooltip must appear on keyboard focus as well as hover. tooltip text: "Token usage for this response" for the token tag. Ensure high contrast and 2px focus ring.
Hana: On token visibility: product asks for per-message token delta in two modes: hover-only or pinned. propose small grey tag near timestamp like "19 tks"; clicking pin toggles persistent visibility for that conversation.
Derek: Implementation: runtime exposes meta.buffered_token_count and meta.token_delta. We'll wire those into the UI. For percent-estimates show a tilde: "~40%" only if estimate_confidence > 0.7. avoid misleading precision.
Jonah: Controls placement debate: floating compact toolbar (right side) vs inline micro-actions under bubble. Suggest responsive rule: if message height > 6 lines -> floating toolbar; else inline. Also use message kebab for minimal UI.
Izzy: Keyboard shortcuts: Resume = Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, Regenerate = Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, Stop = Esc. Show hint in tooltip and inline when space allows. Ensure shortcuts are documented in the keyboard help modal.
Hana: Prompt library integration: if the user used a saved prompt, show a tiny dot and link to the prompt in the message meta. If stream pauses, the chip should surface a small "Edit prompt" quick action that opens the prompt editor with the original template.
Derek: Telemetry: add events: playground.stream_paused (buffered_tokens, can_resume, trigger), playground.resume_clicked (buffered_tokens, trigger), playground.regenerate_clicked (trigger, original_prompt_id?). Keep PII-free.
Jonah: A/B test plan: compare (A) floating toolbar + "Resume" wording vs (B) inline actions + "Regenerate" wording. Metrics: time-to-first-action, help clicks, regen rate, and SR confusion signals (support tickets mentioning "hung").
Izzy: Dev accessibility checklist I'll add to the PR:
- chunkRegion aria-live=polite
- announce once on collapse via role/status region
- chip tabindex=0 + aria-label summarizing tokens and actions
- tooltips visible on focus
- focus ring meets contrast standards
I will include a small code snippet in the spec.
synth-bot: demo branch created: playground/stream-compact-chip-v2 — preview: https://preview.redwood.ai/playground/stream-compact-chip-v2
Hana: Thanks team. Derek please mock responsive behavior in Figma, Jonah add wording to copy doc, Izzy will draft a11y PR notes. aiming for prototype today ~2120001290. Ping here when preview is live :eyes:
